summary: Iffley Airport is a small rural airstrip located in the Gulf Country region of northwestern Queensland, Australia. It primarily supports general aviation operations, cattle station access, and remote pastoral activity in this sparsely populated outback area. The unpaved runway and remote setting make it a typical example of Australia's extensive network of outback airstrips serving the agricultural sector.
faqs:
Q: Does Iffley Airport have scheduled commercial flights?
A: No, Iffley Airport is a small general aviation facility with no scheduled commercial passenger service.

Q: What is the airport primarily used for?
A: It mainly supports cattle station operations, private aircraft, and charter flights serving the surrounding pastoral region.

Q: Are there any passenger facilities at the airport?
A: No, as a remote rural airstrip it has minimal infrastructure and no terminal amenities for travelers.

Q: How remote is Iffley Airport?
A: It is situated in a very isolated part of northwestern Queensland, far from major towns and services.
transport_tips: Access to Iffley Airport typically requires a high-clearance 4WD vehicle on unsealed outback roads, so visitors should travel in convoy and carry recovery gear. Charter or private aircraft are the most reliable way to reach the area, especially during the wet season when roads may become impassable. Plan fuel stops carefully, as the nearest roadhouse or fuel supply can be well over 100 kilometres away.
local_tip: Always carry extra water, fuel, and a satellite communicator or PLB when visiting this region — mobile phone coverage is virtually nonexistent and help can be hours away in an emergency.
